notes: SMALLEST HONEST CHANGE. Exists: a working party-evolution system that decides splits, foundings and how confidently a reason is stated. Missing link: eight numbers deciding it are written in code, and two of them are inline literals rather than even named constants — `allies.length >= 2` and `disputed.length >= 3`. Smallest honest change: move the two inline literals into `PARTY_BODY_CADENCE` beside the other six, so every number that decides party behaviour is in one named place that can be read, argued with and later made content. That is a refactor with no behaviour change and it is the precondition for any of it becoming modder-reachable. What a player would then see: nothing immediately, which is the point — it is the change that makes the next one possible. The behaviour question, what the numbers should be and what they should count, is the part that needs an answer rather than a commit.

PLAYER-FACING INPUT: NONE for any of the eight numbers. Nothing a player presses moves a party's review cadence, committee size, inactivity window, dispute threshold, split-versus-found rule, or the confidence word they read on screen. They are compile-time constants, unreachable from a save and unreachable from a pack.

Two kinds worth keeping apart in the answer, because the fix differs: a number that is arbitrary, where the answer is just a better number or a data field; and a number that is defensible but counts the wrong thing, where a better number fixes nothing. Both of today's fixes were the second kind.

Measured on origin/main at 1c4992e8. PARTY_BODY_CADENCE.repeatedDisputes still reads 2 there. The people-and-life lane's date-guard fix may be on a branch that has not merged; this record reports the threshold, not the state of that fix.

Scope line, agreed with the 'What passing a law actually does' lane: everything downstream of an enacted law is theirs and is absent here. LEGISLATIVE_CADENCE_PROFILE sits on the boundary — it is procedure before enactment rather than effect after it — so it is included, and should be moved if they have already measured it.
This is one of three records from the same sweep. The other two are mod-api-vocabulary-is-two-fields and finished-rooms-waiting-on-a-location.
question: For each threshold below — a number in code that decides an outcome rather than describing one — should it be content a pack can change, a balance parameter the director sets once, or a rule that stays in code? And where a number is defensible but counts the wrong thing, what should it count instead?

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: It gives the clearest examples and settles none of them. PARTY_BODY_CADENCE is a named block of six numbers deciding party behaviour: a review every 3 months, a standing committee of 4, a national committee of 5, a unit inactive after 180 days, and a dispute that must recur at least 2 times before anyone considers leaving. Two more thresholds are not even in that block, but inline literals in the middle of the logic: allies.length >= 2 decides whether leaving is a 'split' or a 'found', and disputed.length >= 3 decides whether the consideration a player reads is labelled 'high' confidence rather than 'medium'. That last one is lamontae's own example, in the code, deciding a word on screen. None of the six is reachable from a content pack.

It is labelled in the source as 'PROPOSED balance parameter, pending the director's confirmation' and carries 3 days between institutional steps and 7 days from referral to a scheduled hearing. It is therefore a known-unconfirmed number that has been running as if confirmed. The comment records that an answer was wanted; nothing records that one arrived.

sourcesChecked.source: A count-comparison sweep across src/simulation and src/presentation
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: It separated structure from judgement, which is the useful part. Most numeric comparisons are structural and not thresholds at all — a decision needs at least 2 options, a merger needs at least 2 organizations, a birth needs 1 or 2 parents — and those belong in code. The ones that read as judgement, and that this record asks about, are the party numbers above, life-personality.ts:137 requiring at least 2 pieces of evidence before personality evidence counts, life-episodes.ts:922 requiring at least 2 non-context anchors, career-path7.ts:404 requiring at least 2 pieces of work history, and life-paths2.ts:1643 requiring at least 10 shifts. Each decides whether something about a person is established or ignored.

title: The bare numbers that decide what a person does, and which of them a modder should own
usableAnswer: A verdict per row: content, balance parameter, or code. For the ones that stay balance parameters, the number he wants. For any row where the count is wrong rather than the number, what it should count — an elapsed window, distinct sittings, distinct questions — since that is what both of today's fixes turned out to be.
whyItMatters: lamontae's example for this category was 'if asking someone three times then makes them say yes, note that'. Two of this exact shape have already been found and fixed today by other lanes: a party breakaway gate that counted two decision records with no date guard, so one afternoon of pressing the same button read as four defeats, and bargainingMannerFromRecord reading three clauses in one sitting as 'strong'. Both were defensible numbers counting the wrong thing. He wants the rest found rather than discovered one playtest at a time. The second half matters just as much: his standing direction is content as data, rules included, and a threshold in a compiled constant is a rule no modder can reach.

answer.summary: Answered as C10, with per-constant dispositions in threshold-dispositions.json. The instruction is to classify each constant by meaning BEFORE moving it anywhere, and every one of the eleven is a number to remove or reclassify rather than a number to confirm. Integrity constraints protect valid state; enacted or profile rules belong to the jurisdiction or organization; simulation response parameters are declared, reviewable model content; a repeated-count shortcut needs a causal replacement. Specifically: the party review interval is work scheduling and is not a cause of dissent or a guarantee of an initiative. Standing-body sizes of 4 and 5 belong to each organization's own governance, not to every party universally. 180 days inactive is a status definition and an evidence-freshness rule; no activity is not dissolution, and continuing obligations stay separate from the decision. Two repeated disputes must become distinct substantive occasions weighed by importance and unresolved reason, with no repeat-click accumulation. allies.length >= 2 must not decide a split: a split is defined by parentage, constituency and an actual organizational founding decision. Three disputed records do not make high confidence, which needs independence, reliability, agreement or contradiction, and relevance rather than a row count. The 3-day step and 7-day hearing should come from a valid scheduling or game profile that preserves the real-date decision, instead of forcing every stage to one delay. Two pieces of personality evidence is wrong because two copies of one event are one observation, and more context is not automatically stronger conviction. Two non-context episode anchors, two work-history rows and ten shifts are all the same error: require the actual roles, causes, tasks, duration and declared conditions instead of a count. The warning that matters most for how this gets fixed: relocating an arbitrary counter to a mod pack is not itself a behavioral repair. Acceptance to request rather than executed: cloning a record, splitting one meeting into more clauses, or repeating the same request with paraphrases must change no substantive outcome on its own, while a genuinely new relevant experience may; and a threshold is only worth testing just below, at and above where the threshold itself has a legitimate named meaning.
